brief.objective: Get the Bandit within 5 m of the Lady while never letting the Guard within 5 m.
brief.approach: Default brief: approach directly, evade the Guard when it closes inside the keep-out radius.

goal.rationale: The Guard sits about 600 m out along the direct line to the Lady, so approach at the capped closing speed and let the fast controller evade if the Guard closes inside the 150 m keep-out.

The Lady is 2556 m away and must be reached within 240 s, so keep closing at the capped speed while the Guard sits about 576 m out and drifts sideways, and let the fast controller evade if it enters the 150 m keep-out.

The Guard sits near y=-578 m with its x drifting toward +108 m, so routing the Bandit via a waypoint offset about 260 m radially inward (x=-160 m) keeps it outside the 150 m keep-out while still closing on the Lady within the remaining 220 s.

The Guard is now at about (123, -475) m and moving along-track toward the Lady at roughly 10 m/s, so this waypoint sits further radially inward at x=-200 m to keep a wider margin than the prior route while still making progress toward the Lady within the remaining 210 s.

The Guard sits near (109, -379) m and drifting toward the Lady, so routing the Bandit along the x=-120 to -165 m side keeps about 230 m lateral separation while the 200 s remaining still allows the required average closing speed of about 11 m/s.

The Guard is about 340 m from the Lady on the bandit's side, so I'm routing via the x=-150 m side to keep roughly 300 m lateral clearance while holding the 12 m/s closing rate needed to reach the Lady within the 190 s remaining.

The Guard is about 300 m from the Lady near the bearing between us, so I'm keeping the x=-150 m detour and the 12 m/s closing cap to hold roughly 200 m of lateral clearance while covering the remaining 1938 m within the 180 s left.

The Guard sits about 250 m from the Lady near x=+60 m, so routing the Bandit through a waypoint offset to x=-150 m keeps roughly 110-200 m of lateral clearance while the 12 m/s cap preserves time to close the remaining 1816 m in 170 s.

The Guard is about 200 m from the Lady (near x=+50, y=-194), not 250 m, and the Bandit is still 1520 m from it, so the offset waypoint at x=-150 keeps roughly 220 m of clearance while the 12 m/s cap leaves enough time for the remaining 1695 m in the 160 s left.

The Guard sits about 152 m from the Lady near x=+43, y=-146, so routing the Bandit through a waypoint offset to negative x keeps the direct line clear of it while the 12 m/s cap still covers the remaining 1573 m in the 150 s left.

The Guard has drifted to about 105 m from the Lady at (40,-97) and is moving +y across the direct line, so I'm keeping the Bandit on an offset path toward negative x that stays about 165 m from the Guard while still reaching the Lady within the remaining 140 s at the 12 m/s cap.

The Guard is now about 63 m from the Lady at (40,-49) and the Bandit is still 1332 m out with 130 s left, so I'm holding the offset waypoint at (-120,-40) to keep clear of the Guard while the Bandit closes at up to 12 m/s.

The Guard is passing the Lady at about 44 m along-track and moving away at 4.8 m/s, so I'm keeping the offset waypoint at (-120,-40) to route the Bandit around it while closing at up to 12 m/s with 120 s left.

The Guard is drifting ahead along-track at about 4.8 m/s, so I'm routing the Bandit on the radial-negative side toward a near-Lady waypoint at (-80,-30), keeping well clear of the Guard's track while using the 15 m/s closing cap to finish the approach in the remaining 110 s.

The Bandit is already closing on the Lady at about 15 m/s with the Guard 95 m off to the side of the Lady's far track, so a direct glide-slope approach finishes sooner than the detour waypoint, which would only leave the Bandit 80 m short of the win radius with little time left.

The Guard is now about 160 m from the Lady on the far side from the Bandit's approach track, so the direct glide-slope approach keeps the Bandit's closing time within the remaining 90 s and the Guard stays behind the Lady, while the Bandit's closing speed is capped at 12 m/s.

The Guard is about 210 m from the Lady on the far side from the Bandit and moving away, with 910 m separation from the Bandit, so a direct glide-slope approach at 12 m/s closing speed still reaches the Lady within the remaining 80 s without passing the Guard.

The Guard is about 260 m from the Lady, offset roughly 40 m from the Bandit's approach line and drifting away along-track, so a direct approach at a reduced 8 m/s closing speed should reach the Lady in the remaining 70 s while keeping clear of the Guard.

The Guard is about 315 m past the Lady on the far side and receding, so the Bandit's approach from the -y side is clear, and with 60 s left at 468 m we need a faster closing speed of 10 m/s to reach the Lady in time, with a 5 m standoff to satisfy the win condition.

The Guard is about 740 m from the Bandit on the far (+y) side of the Lady, so the direct -y approach is clear, and with 50 s left and 380 m to go we need about 8 m/s average closing, so approach at 10 m/s and tighten the standoff to 5 m for the win condition.

The Lady is 282 m away with 40 s left, and the Guard is about 640 m from the Bandit and on the far side, so a direct glide at 10 m/s closing with a 5 m standoff covers the remaining distance in time while still leaving room to brake for the final approach.

The Bandit is 184 m from the Lady with 30 s left and the Guard is 537 m away and not closing fast, so continue the direct approach at 10 m/s closing, then brake to final approach speed inside about 60 m before the standoff.

The Bandit is 105 m from the Lady with 20 s left and the Guard is 456 m away and not inside keep-out, so keep closing directly but cap closing speed at 8 m/s and brake toward the 5 m standoff to avoid overshooting.

The Bandit is about 58 m from the Lady with 10 s left and the Guard is 406 m away, so keep closing directly but cap closing speed at 4 m/s so the Bandit brakes onto the 5 m standoff before time runs out without overshooting.
